metaDescription: Six propane pyramid patio heaters compared on BTU, flame tube design, tilt and flame-out safety, base stability and covers for your yard.
introParagraphs: A pyramid patio heater is the glass tower you see at restaurants: a tall four-sided frame with a flame burning inside a clear tube, radiating heat out from the pyramid top. It looks like a feature piece and delivers a lot of warmth to a wide circle. It is also big, tall and tippy if the base is skimpy, so safety shutoffs and a stable base matter more here than with any other style.

This lineup covers six propane pyramids. The DWVO is 89 inches with side panels and a 200 square foot coverage claim, the Pamapic is 89 inches with a weighted base and triple safety protection, the Hykolity is 90 inches rated at 48,000 BTU, the Tangkula is rated at 45,000 BTU with a 17 foot heat range and CSA certification, the FOOWIN uses aluminum and stainless steel, and the PATIOPIA adds pulse ignition and a cover. All are outdoor-only fuel-burning heaters.

We evaluated each one based on product specs and buyer feedback, concentrating on output, safety systems, base design and extras. Check overhead clearance, since these towers need far more headroom than a tabletop heater.

products.name: DWVO 48,000 BTU Pyramid Patio Heater With Side Panels

specList.label: Safety
specList.value: Tilt sensor, flame-out, auto shut-off valve

products.description:
The DWVO delivers 48,000 BTU of steady infrared warmth across up to 200 square feet, according to the listing. Integrated side panels give you surfaces for coffee, drinks, snacks and phones, with a decorative cutout pattern. A tilt sensor, flame-out protection and an automatic shut-off valve provide layered control, and the frame is stainless steel around an enclosed glass flame tube.

Built-in wheels make it easier to reposition as your layout changes, and a PVC cover shields it from rain, dust and debris between uses. Electronic ignition starts it, and an adjustable control knob moves from gentle background warmth to stronger heating. The tradeoff is that at 89 inches it needs generous headroom, and the listing gives no weight or ballast detail. Stainless and glass also need regular wiping to keep the tower looking clean.

In ownership terms, expect to keep the PVC cover on when the heater is cool and to leave plenty of clearance on every side. Compared with the Pamapic, it documents the tilt and flame-out sensors but lists no weighted base. Compared with the Tangkula at 45,000 BTU, it has 3,000 BTU more and a stated 200 square foot claim against a 17 foot range. It suits buyers who want a drinks surface and layered shutoffs.
products.bestFor: Dining and conversation areas where drink surfaces and layered safety matter.
pros: Tilt sensor, flame-out and shut-off valve
Side panels for drinks and phones
cons: No base weight or ballast listed

products.name: Pamapic 89 Inch Pyramid Patio Heater With Quartz Tube
products.description:
The Pamapic is an 89 inch propane flame tower with a quartz glass tube, running on a standard 20 pound tank that is not included. It uses pulse ignition with no matches or electricity, and a side-access door makes tank changes quick. Triple safety protection covers a tip-over auto shut-off valve, flame-failure protection and an overheat guard.

The listing credits a stable weighted base with keeping the tower secure on a patio, deck or porch, which is the most important feature on a tall pyramid. It claims coverage up to a 15-foot diameter by concentrating heat at the top and dispersing it outward. The tradeoff is that the 15 foot figure is smaller than the 18-foot claims on many tabletop towers, and the BTU rating is not given in the excerpt. A custom-fit fade-resistant cover is included.

In ownership terms, plan for about an hour of assembly with pre-fitted parts and illustrated instructions, and smooth wheels move it between patio and poolside. Compared with the DWVO at a 200 square foot claim, it lists a ballast-style base but no side panels. Compared with the Hykolity at 90 inches, it is a touch shorter and adds the overheat guard. It suits windy decks and poolsides.
products.bestFor: Windy decks and poolsides where a planted base matters.

products.name: Hykolity 48,000 BTU Pyramid Patio Heater With Cover

specList.label: Run time
specList.value: 8 to 10 hours on a 20 lb tank

products.description:
The Hykolity Pyramid is rated at 48,000 BTU, stands 90 inches tall and uses a standard 20 pound propane tank that is not included. It has a variable heat setting with a built-in control valve so you can adjust the warmth. The listing says a full tank can run it continuously for 8 to 10 hours.

A side door gives easy access to change the tank, and two detachable wheels let you move it. The glass tube shows a flame inside, which adds a decorative touch to the yard. An anti-tilt device shuts the heater off past 45 degrees, and a waterproof cover protects it in bad weather. The tradeoff is that the excerpt lists no flame-out valve and no ballast, so confirm those before you buy. At 90 inches it is the tallest tower here.

In ownership terms, the cover is the daily-life feature, because covered storage keeps the glass and reflector clean between parties. Compared with the DWVO at 89 inches, it is slightly taller and has fewer documented sensors. Compared with the Tangkula at 45,000 BTU, it adds 3,000 BTU but not the CSA certification. It suits buyers who want a standard 48,000 BTU pyramid with a cover.
products.bestFor: Open spaces with high clearance that want a cover included.
pros: 8 to 10 hours on a 20 lb tank
cons: 90 inch tower needs the most headroom

products.name: Tangkula 45,000 BTU Pyramid Patio Heater With Cover
products.description:
The Tangkula is rated at 45,000 BTU with a 17 foot heat range, the lowest output here but with a clearly stated range. It is CSA certified, and the 360 degree heat needs no preheating. Triple safety protection combines an anti-tilt device that shuts off past 45 degrees, flame-out protection and oxygen depletion protection.

The listing mentions an aluminum reflector top cover and a heat-resistant glass tube, plus a magnetic door for easier tank access. A fast pulse ignition lights the flame with a button press, and a variable control knob adjusts the output from low to high. A zippered cover and smooth wheels are included. The tradeoff is that the ignition needs one AAA battery, which is not included, and the listing gives no base weight or exact height.

In ownership terms, keep a spare AAA battery on hand and store the heater under its cover. Compared with the DWVO at 48,000 BTU, it gives up 3,000 BTU but lists a certification and an oxygen sensor the DWVO excerpt does not. Compared with the FOOWIN at a 130 square foot claim, it gives a distance figure instead of an area. It suits smaller patios where certification matters.
products.bestFor: Smaller patios where a certification and oxygen sensor matter.

products.name: FOOWIN 48,000 BTU Pyramid Patio Heater With Wheels

specList.label: Coverage
specList.value: 130 sq ft, heats in about 5 minutes

products.description:
The FOOWIN is a 48,000 BTU pyramid heater built mainly from aluminum and stainless steel, which the listing says gives good corrosion resistance. The heat is said to spread within 130 square feet and warm up in about 5 minutes. Built-in wheels on the base let you move it anywhere.

An auto-shutoff turns the flame off if the tower tilts more than 45 degrees, and the listing also mentions an explosion-proof pipe and protective nets. It adds that each unit went through 10,000 automatic flame-out tests at the factory. A waterproof cover and operating gloves come in the box, and a one-touch ignition and control valve make it easy to light. The tradeoff is the modest 130 square foot claim, which is the smallest area figure in the lineup.

In ownership terms, the gloves are a nice touch for handling a hot reflector, and the cover keeps rain out of the tube. Compared with the DWVO at a 200 square foot claim, it covers less area for the same 48,000 BTU. Compared with the Tangkula at 17 feet, it lacks a stated certification. It suits wet climates.
products.bestFor: Rain-prone patios where corrosion resistance matters.
pros: Flame-out testing claim at the factory

products.name: PATIOPIA Flame Pyramid Patio Heater With Cover
products.description:
The PATIOPIA is a flame pyramid heater with a user-friendly pulse ignition system, variable heat settings and a built-in control valve. The listing says a tip-over protection system includes a safety valve that shuts the unit off if it tilts. At 89.4 inches tall, it shows a glass flame tube as its centerpiece.

A cover made from fade-resistant fabric is included, and it zips open and closed for covered patios. Durable wheels let you roll it, and the same listing family offers black, brown and stainless versions. The tradeoff is that the excerpt does not state BTU, coverage or a flame-out valve, so you cannot compare output directly. The tip-over valve is the only documented shutoff.

In ownership terms, ignition is simple and the cover helps with seasonal storage. Compared with the DWVO, it documents fewer safety layers and has no side panels. Compared with the Pamapic, it lists no weighted base and no overheat guard, and it is 0.4 inches taller. It suits buyers who want easy ignition and a simple cover-included tower.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a simple pulse-ignition tower with a cover.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Pyramid heaters radiate from the top, so heat spreads in a wide circle rather than a narrow beam. Claims differ in format: the DWVO says 200 square feet, the Tangkula says a 17 foot range, the Pamapic says a 15-foot diameter and the FOOWIN says 130 square feet. Treat them as the maker's figures and plan on seating within about 6 to 8 feet of the tower for real warmth. A 48,000 BTU model such as the Hykolity delivers more than the Tangkula at 45,000 BTU.

A glass-tube pyramid is tall, so a tilt shutoff is not optional. The Tangkula, FOOWIN and Hykolity list a 45 degree tilt cutoff, the DWVO adds flame-out and an automatic shut-off valve, and the Pamapic lists a tip-over valve, flame-failure protection and an overheat guard. The Tangkula alone lists CSA certification and oxygen depletion protection. Prefer a heater that documents at least tilt and flame-out protection.

A 89 to 90 inch tower is a sail in a gust, so the base decides whether it stays upright. The Pamapic is the one pick that credits a stable weighted base, while the others do not state ballast. Wheels make movement easy but cut stability, so lock or place them on level ground. Never place a pyramid on a slope, and consider anchoring or placing it in a corner out of the wind.

The Hykolity is 90 inches, the Pamapic and DWVO 89, and the PATIOPIA 89.4, so all of them stand well over 7 feet tall. Heat rises from the top reflector, so you need overhead clearance well beyond the 8 foot mark under a roof, awning or pergola. The manual's distances come first, and many covered patios cannot satisfy them. Measure the ceiling, tree branches and umbrella tops before you buy.

A pulse or electronic igniter beats a match, but some need a battery. The Tangkula needs one AAA battery, while the Pamapic and PATIOPIA use pulse ignition without a battery mention, and the DWVO uses electronic ignition. A variable control valve lets you dial down the flame to save propane. Keep a lighter on hand in case the igniter fails.

A cover protects the glass tube and reflector from rain, dust and pollen. The DWVO includes a PVC cover, the Hykolity a waterproof cover, the Tangkula and PATIOPIA zippered covers, and the FOOWIN a waterproof cover with gloves. The FOOWIN's aluminum and stainless build resists corrosion best of the group. Always let the heater cool before covering it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Output and coverage
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated BTU and coverage claims. The DWVO, Hykolity and FOOWIN list 48,000 BTU, the Tangkula lists 45,000 BTU, and the Pamapic and PATIOPIA give no BTU in the excerpt. Coverage figures differ in format, so we treated them as the maker's claims.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked documented shutoffs and certification. The Pamapic lists three layers, the DWVO lists tilt and flame-out, the Tangkula adds CSA and oxygen depletion protection, and the PATIOPIA lists only a tip-over valve.

howWeEvaluated.title: Base and stability
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for any ballast or weighted-base detail. The Pamapic lists a stable weighted base, while the other five do not state one. Tall towers with no stated ballast lost points.

howWeEvaluated.title: Extras and covers
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared what ships in the box. The DWVO has side panels and a PVC cover, the FOOWIN adds gloves, the Tangkula and PATIOPIA add zippered covers, and the Hykolity includes a waterproof cover.

howWeEvaluated.title: Materials and value
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed finish and build. The FOOWIN uses aluminum and stainless steel, the DWVO a stainless frame, and the Tangkula an aluminum reflector top. Value credit went to stated certifications and complete safety documentation.

cards.label: Weighted base
cards.text: A heavy foot resists tipping and is the right choice on a deck with wind. The Pamapic 89 Inch Pyramid Patio Heater With Quartz Tube lists one. Choose it for exposed spots and accept that it is harder to shift.

cards.label: Lighter frame
cards.text: Aluminum is easier to move but less planted, so sheltered use suits it. The FOOWIN 48,000 BTU Pyramid Patio Heater With Wheels and Tangkula 45,000 BTU Pyramid Patio Heater With Cover use aluminum and wheels. Choose it for easy repositioning.

howToChoose.note: Weight for stability, light for mobility.

faq.q: How much clearance does a pyramid heater need?
faq.a: More than most buyers expect. Towers such as the 90 inch Hykolity and 89 inch DWVO stand over 7 feet tall, and heat rises from the top reflector. Follow the manual's distances from roofs, awnings and tree branches, and do not place one under a low covered porch.

faq.q: How long will a tank last?
faq.a: The Hykolity listing says a 20 pound tank runs it for 8 to 10 hours continuously at full output. Turning the variable heat down stretches that time. Keep a spare tank on hand for long gatherings.

faq.q: Is a pyramid heater safe on a wooden deck?
faq.a: It can be if you follow the clearance and base guidance, but the glass tube and reflector get very hot. Choose a stable base such as the Pamapic's weighted foot and keep the tower away from railings and furniture. Check that the deck surface is level and non-combustible if the manual requires it.

faq.q: Why does my igniter not light?
faq.a: The Tangkula needs one AAA battery for its pulse igniter, so replace it first. Check that the tank valve is open and the regulator is connected. Keep a long lighter in case the electronic igniter fails.

faq.q: Should I buy a model with a certification?
faq.a: A certification mark such as the Tangkula's CSA listing is a useful trust signal, because it shows the design met a safety standard. Most other listings in this group do not state one. Read the product page rather than assuming.

faq.q: Do I need to cover it?
faq.a: Yes, use the cover when the heater is cool and not in use. The DWVO, Hykolity, Tangkula, PATIOPIA and FOOWIN all include one. Covers keep rain and dust out of the glass tube and reflector.

faq.q: Can it work in the wind?
faq.a: Pyramids radiate in all directions, so they lose less than a focused heater, but gusts still blow the flame around. Place the tower in a corner or beside a wall of the house, and pick the weighted Pamapic for exposed spots. Do not run any gas heater in strong wind.
